messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT · severity=P2 · service=hosted-runtime/kvcache
incident-bot: metric=kvcache.memory.used_pct crossed 92% in us-west-2 cluster for model-redwood-7b-v2. Auto-escalation: paging on-call. Link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/2181234567 :rotating_light:

sre-jamie: saw this spike. OOMs showing on 3 nodes. Memory growth looks correlated with a small subset of requests with extremely long contexts (>120k tokens).

alice-runtime: looking at trace ids — continuous-batching appears to be coalescing many long sessions, KV windows never evicting because eviction threshold was incorrectly set to 0.75 in the dynamic-evict policy after yesterday's config push. That plus prefix caching of prompts causing runaway KV growth.

bob-eng: uhoh. which rollout? I pushed a change to dynamic-evict last night but I set a tighter threshold, not looser. Can you paste the effective config?

alice-runtime: here's the effective config from the nodes (abridged):
```
model: redwood-7b-v2
continuous_batching: enabled
dynamic_eviction: enabled
eviction_threshold: 0.75  # expected 0.35 in prod, drifted after merge
max_prefetch_entries: 20000
```

carol-support: customers seeing 503s and higher latency. Support ticket queue shows ~18 reports in the last 20m, mostly from chat sessions with very long system prompts. CS priority: medium-high.

sre-jamie: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable continuous_batching for this model in us-west-2 (fast) 2) roll back dynamic_eviction to 0.35 3) trigger graceful KV eviction job to free memory 4) scale up dedicated pool by 2 nodes if OOMs persist.

bob-eng: I can flip the dynamic_eviction flag now and push a hotfix for the config. Doing a dry-run toggle on one node first.

alice-runtime: dry-run looks good — eviction is reclaiming large prefixes. Memory used_pct dropped from 94% to 68% on the node.

sre-jamie: ok proceeding with region-wide toggle: `/infra toggle-config --service hosted-runtime --model redwood-7b-v2 continuous_batching=false --region us-west-2`

platform-ops: FYI I'm warming two spare nodes in us-west-2 in case scaling is needed. ETA ~6m.

bob-eng: rolled back eviction_threshold to 0.35 across cluster. Confirming propagation.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: disable_continuous_batching, rollback_eviction_threshold, start_eviction_job, warm_nodes.

alice-runtime: eviction job running. Quick log tail:
```
[evict] reclaimed 4.2GB from prefix-cache in 00:21
[evict] reclaimed 3.6GB from long-session entries
[mem] used_pct now 61% on average
```

carol-support: customer-impact update: affected customers are mostly sandbox/test tenants and three small production customers on dev-stage routes. No enterprise SLAs breached at this time. Notifying the three customers via standard incident template now.

sre-jamie: monitoring — memory and OOM alerts cleared on first wave. Latency improved for the noisy sessions. Leaving continuous_batching disabled until we can push a safer config.

bob-eng: root cause hypothesis: a recent infra merge accidentally set default eviction threshold to 0.75 for models with high prefetch limits. Combined with long prompts and continuous_batching, KV entries accumulated faster than eviction could keep up.

alice-runtime: remediation next steps: 1) write a canary that simulates long-context sessions to validate eviction config under load 2) add a hard memory cap per-session to limit prefix kv growth 3) add alert that triggers when a single trace accounts for >30% of new KV entries in a 10m window.

platform-ops: why did continuous_batching make it worse vs before?

alice-runtime: continuous batching coalesces user streams into larger micro-batches to improve GPU utilization. For normal prompts that's fine. For these very long sessions, coalescing kept KV caches warm across sessions and prevented ephemeral eviction. With higher eviction_threshold we never reclaimed the stale prefixes.

sre-jamie: handoff: paging window ends in 1h, I'll stay until then and then hand off to @bob-eng for overnight ops. Bob — you'll have runbook steps in the incident doc. Confirm please.

bob-eng: confirmed. Runbook highlights: 1) if mem >85% after evictions, enable extra nodes and notify infra 2) if evictions don't reclaim within 10m, kill continuous_batching on global service 3) collect traces for top 20 memory-allocating sessions and attach to ticket.

carol-support: sent customer notifications and created a follow-up playbook for affected tenants. Linking ticket list: https://support.redwood/tickets?q=2181234567

alice-runtime: filed a PR to set safer default eviction_threshold=0.35 and to gate continuous_batching for sessions >50k tokens. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/merge/7654

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE · status=mitigated · summary=memory reclaimed via eviction + continuous_batching disabled · impacted_customers=3 · next_steps=postmortem + config PR verification

sre-jamie: closing notes before handoff: all nodes stable, metrics holding, watchers on for 2h. Will attach logs and timeline to the incident doc. Thanks all for the quick triage. :raised_hands:

bob-eng: thanks — I'll pick this up at handoff and run the canary overnight.

carol-support: closing customer comms loop once postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall -> bob-eng at 2181234620
